title: Resolution urging Congress to add warning labels to food nutrition labels
summary: This resolution calls on the United States Congress to pass, and the President to sign, legislation requiring nutrition labels on food and drink products to include consumer education markings, such as warnings for high sugar, salt, saturated fat or calories. It cites examples like Chile's hexagonal warning labels and the United Kingdom's traffic light labeling system as models. The resolution notes that 26.8 percent of New Yorkers citywide and 37.4 percent of Bronx residents have a body mass index of 30.0 or higher.
